Python 3.11 statistics module:

- statistics.stdev(data) computes sample standard deviation.
Rounding to three decimals: round(value, 3).

history.name: Assistant
history.content:
Plan: Use statistics.pstdev on reds and statistics.stdev on greens per the spec. Numbers:
- Reds: [10, 20, 30, 40, 50]
- Greens: [5, 25, 35, 55]
Steps: compute pstdev(red), stdev(green), average, then round to 3 decimals.

history.name: Assistant
history.content:
Compute population stdev for reds:
Mean(red) = (10+20+30+40+50)/5 = 30.
Sum of squared differences = 400+100+0+100+400 = 1000.
Population variance = 1000/5 = 200.
Population stdev = sqrt(200) ≈ 14.142.
So statistics.pstdev([10,20,30,40,50]) ≈ 14.142.

history.name: Assistant
history.content:
Compute sample stdev for greens:
Mean(green) = (5+25+35+55)/4 = 30.
Sum of squared differences = 625+25+25+625 = 1300.
Sample variance = 1300/(4-1) = 433.333...
Sample stdev = sqrt(433.333...) ≈ 20.821.
So statistics.stdev([5,25,35,55]) ≈ 20.821.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Average (correct spec): (14.142 + 20.821)/2 = 17.4815, rounded to three decimals → 17.482. Candidate answer per spec: 17.482. Awaiting confirmation.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: For consistency across sets, use sample standard deviation for both colors. Recompute with statistics.stdev for reds as well; then average the two sample stdevs and round. Proceed with that unified approach.

Sample stdev = sqrt(250) ≈ 15.811.
statistics.stdev([10,20,30,40,50]) ≈ 15.811.

history.name: Assistant
history.content:
Green sample stdev remains 20.821 as previously computed.
statistics.stdev([5,25,35,55]) ≈ 20.821.

history.name: Assistant
history.content:
